summary: This document defines a collection of common data types for the YANG data modeling language, including new type definitions. It obsoletes RFC 6991.

eli5.summary: Building blocks like dates and addresses get reused everywhere, so this provides a shared box of them for YANG models.

questions: what is the yang counter32 type
subtitle: A shared toolbox of ready-made data types, such as counters, dates, IP addresses and host names, for YANG models.

tldr.problem: Every YANG data model needs the same basic building blocks, such as counters, timestamps, IP addresses and domain names. Without a shared definition, each model would define them differently.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9911 defines two YANG modules, ietf-yang-types and ietf-inet-types, that hold these common derived types, with patterns, ranges and rules for how values are written.
tldr.outcome: It is the second revision of the types first published in RFC 6021. It adds new types such as date, time, language-tag and email-address, and it obsoletes RFC 6991.

today: RFC 9911 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 6991. It is the current definition of the two common types modules according to the unit metadata, which lists no later RFC obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why Common Types Exist
sections.content:
YANG is a data modeling language used to model configuration and state data manipulated by the Network Configuration Protocol (NETCONF). It has a small set of built-in data types and lets authors derive new types from them.

RFC 9911 collects the derived types that many models need. They live in two modules. The ietf-yang-types module has generally useful types: counters and gauges, date and time types, and common string values such as UUIDs, dotted-quad notation and language tags. The ietf-inet-types module has types for the Internet Protocol suite: IP addresses, domain names, host names, URIs, email addresses and values of common protocol fields such as port numbers.

This is the second revision of the work first published as RFC 6021. The first revision, RFC 6991, added several types. RFC 9911 adds more, addresses Erratum IDs 4076 and 5105, aligns the yang-identifier definition with YANG 1.1, and improves some pattern statements. New types may be proposed to the NETMOD Working Group.
sections.eli5: Imagine every LEGO builder inventing their own brick shape. Nothing would fit. This document is the official box of standard bricks that YANG builders share.

sections.title: The Type Catalogue and SMIv2 Equivalents
sections.content:
Section 2 lists every type in the two modules with its base type and the RFC that introduced it (RFC 6021, RFC 6991 or RFC 9911). For example, counter32 is based on uint32 and came from RFC 6021, while date is based on string and is new in RFC 9911.

It also maps many types to equivalent SMIv2 types, the data type system of SNMP management information bases. A YANG type is equivalent when the two have the same set of values and the semantics of the values are equivalent. Examples from the tables: counter32 matches Counter32, mac-address matches MacAddress, port-number matches InetPortNumber and language-tag matches LangTag.
sections.eli5: The catalogue is like the index of a parts box, telling you which part is new and which older measuring systems have a matching part.

sections.title: Counters, Gauges and Identifiers
sections.content:
A counter32 is a non-negative integer that only goes up until it reaches 2^32-1 (4294967295), then wraps to zero. counter64 does the same up to 2^64-1. A single counter value carries little information by itself, since counters have no defined initial value. The text says counters should not be used for configuration nodes and that a default statement SHOULD NOT be used with them.

A zero-based-counter32 or zero-based-counter64 does have a defined initial value of zero. A management station must know the minimum time to wrap and the real time between polls, and discard data if the actual time is too long.

gauge32 and gauge64 are non-negative integers that may rise or fall but stay between a minimum and a maximum. If the thing being measured goes past the maximum, the gauge simply sits at its maximum.

For identifiers, object-identifier holds administratively assigned names in a registration tree, written as dot-separated numbers. It is not limited to 128 sub-identifiers, so object-identifier-128 SHOULD be used to represent the SMIv2 OBJECT IDENTIFIER type. yang-identifier follows the YANG 1.1 identifier rule: it starts with a letter or underscore, followed by letters, digits, underscores, hyphens or dots.
sections.eli5: A counter is like a car odometer that only goes up and rolls over to zero at the end. A gauge is like a fuel gauge that can go up and down but never past full or empty.

sections.title: Dates, Times and Durations
sections.content:
RFC 9911 adds several time types. date-and-time is a profile of ISO 8601 defined by the date-time production in RFC 3339, updated by RFC 9557. A seconds value of 60 is allowed only for leap seconds. The new date and time types carry an optional time zone offset, and date-no-zone and time-no-zone drop it.

The offset Z means the value is in UTC and the local time zone is unknown, while +00:00 means it is in UTC and the local time zone reference point is UTC. Values with a known time zone use a numeric offset calculated from the device's configured offset, so they can change when a server follows daylight saving time.

The new duration types are hours32, minutes32, seconds32, centiseconds32, milliseconds32, microseconds32, microseconds64, nanoseconds32 and nanoseconds64. Each states the range it can express and should be range-restricted to 0..max where negative durations make no sense.

The older timeticks type counts hundredths of a second between two epochs, and timestamp records the timeticks value at which something happened. A timestamp must be reset to zero when the associated timeticks node wraps around after 497+ days.
sections.eli5: Dates and times are like writing down when something happened, with or without the name of your time zone. Durations are stopwatches that count in hours, seconds or even tiny fractions of a second.

sections.title: Addresses, Prefixes and Protocol Fields
sections.content:
The ietf-inet-types module covers protocol fields first. ip-version is an enumeration. dscp is a Differentiated Services Code Point restricted to 0..63. ipv6-flow-label is restricted to 0..1048575. port-number covers 0..65535 for transport protocols such as UDP, TCP, DCCP or SCTP; port zero is reserved by IANA and can be excluded by subtyping. New in this revision are protocol-number, an 8-bit value from the IPv4 protocol field or IPv6 next header field, and upper-layer-protocol-number, the number in the last next header field of a chain of IPv6 extension headers.

as-number is a uint32 with no range restriction so it supports the 32-bit autonomous system number space.

ip-address is a union of ipv4-address and ipv6-address and allows a zone index after a % sign. The -no-zone variants forbid the zone index. The new -link-local variants cover IPv4 addresses in 169.254.0.0/16 and IPv6 addresses in fe80::/10.

Prefix types such as ipv4-prefix and ipv6-prefix accept values whose non-prefix bits are not zero, but implementations have to return the canonical form with those bits zeroed. For example, 192.0.2.1/24 becomes 192.0.2.0/24. The new ip-address-and-prefix types keep both an address and a prefix length together.
sections.eli5: An address is a house number, a prefix is the name of the whole street, and a port is the door of a particular flat in the building.

sections.title: Domain Names, Host Names, URIs and Email
sections.content:
domain-name is a DNS name from 1 to 253 characters. The DNS protocol limits encoded names to 255 characters, but because of the length bytes and trailing NUL byte only 253 characters fit in the dotted textual form. It does not support wildcards or classless in-addr.arpa delegations. Values use ASCII, the canonical form is lowercase, and internationalized names MUST be A-labels as defined in RFC 5890. A schema node that uses it MUST describe when and how the name is resolved to IP addresses.

The new host-name type is a stricter domain name for fully qualified host names, and the host union now uses host-name in place of domain-name. The uri type holds URIs and MUST be ASCII and normalized.

The new email-address type is an internationalized email address that follows the addr-spec rule of RFC 5322, extended by RFC 6532. Implementations MUST support the RFC 6532 internationalization extensions, but support for the obsolete RFC 5322 forms is not required.
sections.eli5: A domain name is the name of a website on a street sign, and an email address is the name of a mailbox. These types make sure everybody writes those names in the same careful way.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The document reuses the URIs for ietf-yang-types and ietf-inet-types in the IETF XML Registry. IANA updated the YANG Module Names registry so that both modules reference RFC 9911 instead of RFC 6991. The registrations are: ietf-yang-types with namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-yang-types and prefix yang, and ietf-inet-types with namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-inet-types and prefix inet.
sections.eli5: IANA is the librarian. It changed the library cards for these two modules so they now point to the new edition of the book.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that the definitions themselves have no security impact on the Internet, but that the use of these definitions in concrete YANG modules might have. The security considerations of the YANG specification, RFC 7950, apply to this document as well.
sections.eli5: The bricks themselves are harmless. What matters is what people build with them, so builders still have to follow the safety rules of YANG.
